Laxmi Prasad Devkota ("The Great Poet" / Mahakavi: "Muna Madan", the best-selling book in Nepali literature); Parijat ("Siris ko Phool" / The Blue Mimosa); modern authors Samrat Upadhyay and Manjushree Thapa.), and sports (Cricket is an immense national passion (the Nepali national cricket team "Rhinos" qualified for the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in 2024 amidst wild domestic euphoria); Football (packed Dasharath Stadium); Mountaineering and Trail Running (world-record mountain athlete Mira Rai; Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja who summited all 14 eight-thousanders in 6 months); Volleyball (national sport).).

name: North Korea
nationalDay: September 9 (Day of the Foundation of the Republic in 1948)
motto: Powerful and Prosperous Nation (강성대국 - Gangseong Daeguk)
borders: South Korea (divided by the 4 km wide Demilitarized Zone / DMZ along the 38th parallel)
coastline: 2,495 km (Sea of Japan / East Sea of Korea to the east, and Yellow Sea / West Sea of Korea to the west)
highestPoint: Paektu Mountain (Mount Paektu, 2,744 m - sacred active stratovolcano on the Chinese border, cradling Heaven Lake)
lowestPoint: Sea of Japan / Yellow Sea (0 m)
longestRiver: Amnok River (Yalu River, 790 km along Chinese border) / Duman River (Tumen River, 521 km) / Taedong River (flows through Pyongyang)
majorLakes: Heaven Lake (Lake Chon - breathtaking volcanic caldera lake atop Mount Paektu)
majorMountains: Mount Kumgang (Diamond Mountain, 1,638 m - famed for dramatic granite pinnacles)
climate: Humid continental; short, hot, humid summers and long, bitterly cold, snowy winters influenced by Siberian air masses
naturalHazards: Severe droughts followed by seasonal monsoon flash flooding causing agricultural crop damage
Spring dust storms from the Gobi
environmentalIssues: Deforestation on hillside slopes from past wood-fuel harvesting
Soil erosion and land degradation impacting cereal crop yields
Air pollution from heavy coal-fired industrial heating
biodiversity: Rugged mountain forests harbor the Siberian (Amur) tiger, Amur leopard, Asiatic black bear, Manchurian sika deer, red-crowned crane, and pristine subalpine flora around Mount Paektu
languages: Korean (Munhwa'ŏ / Cultural Language - official state standard)
government: Unitary one-party socialist state / totalitarian hereditary dictatorship
headOfState: President of State Affairs Kim Jong Un (General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea); Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly Choe Ryong Hae (represents state diplomatically)
legislature: Supreme People's Assembly (SPA - unicameral 687-seat parliament)
constitution: Adopted in 1972; amended repeatedly (incorporating Juche, Songun, and nuclear state status, with Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism as state ideology)
mainPoliticalParties: Workers' Party of Korea (WPK - sole ruling party)
Democratic Front for the Reunification of Korea (including minor satellite groups: Korean Social Democratic Party, Chondoist Chongu Party)
latestElections: 14th Supreme People's Assembly election in March 2019; 8th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea in 2021
politicalSituation: Under Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un, North Korea has consolidated its status as a de facto nuclear-weapon state, enshrining nuclear status irrevocably in its constitution and advancing intercontinental ballistic missiles (Hwasong-17/18), hypersonic gliders, and military reconnaissance satellites. In 2024, North Korea formally abandoned the long-standing goal of peaceful reunification with South Korea, declaring the South its "principal enemy", and signed a historic Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty with Russia in June 2024 (including a mutual defense assistance pact), expanding geopolitical and military cooperation.
foreignRelations: Deep strategic, military, and economic alliance with the Russian Federation (formal mutual defense pact signed in 2024); comprehensive friendship and economic trade lifeline with China; adversarial relations with the United States, South Korea, and Japan; subject to comprehensive UN Security Council sanctions.
military: Korean People's Army (KPA: Ground Force, Navy, Air and Anti-Air Force, Strategic Rocket Force, and Special Operation Force; world's 4th largest active standing military with ~1.2 million personnel; nuclear weapons capability and extensive artillery batteries).
internationalOrgs: UN (admitted simultaneously with South Korea in 1991)
adminDivisions: 9 provinces (do), 1 direct-administered city (Pyongyang), 3 special cities (Nampo, Rason, Kaesong)
history: Korean civilization traces to the mythical founding of Gojoseon by Dangun in 2333 BC. The Three Kingdoms of Korea (Goguryeo, Baekje, and Silla) competed for supremacy; northern Goguryeo was renowned for military power and vast Manchurian territories. Following unified Silla and the Goryeo Dynasty (which gave Korea its Western name and invented metal movable type in 1234), the Joseon Dynasty (1392–1910) established Confucian statecraft and King Sejong the Great created the Hangul alphabet in 1443. Following the Japanese annexation of Korea in 1910 and brutal colonial rule, Kim Il Sung led anti-Japanese guerrilla resistance in Manchuria. At the conclusion of World War II in 1945, the Korean Peninsula was divided along the 38th parallel into Soviet and American occupation zones. The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was proclaimed on September 9, 1948, under Kim Il Sung. On June 25, 1950, North Korea launched a full-scale invasion of the South, starting the devastating Korean War (1950–1953). UN forces led by the US intervened on behalf of the South, while the Chinese People's Volunteer Army intervened for the North. The war ended on July 27, 1953, with an armistice (not a permanent peace treaty), establishing the heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). Kim Il Sung established the autarkic ideology of Juche (self-reliance), centralizing power through the Chollima economic movement. Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, North Korea endured a catastrophic famine in the 1990s ("The Arduous March"). Kim Jong Il instituted the "Songun" (military-first) doctrine and conducted North Korea's first nuclear test in 2006. Kim Jong Un assumed power in December 2011, accelerating missile and nuclear miniaturization programs.
recentEvents2020_2026: North Korea maintained near-total international border closures during 2020–2023, subsequently reopening trade with China and Russia. In September 2023, Kim Jong Un traveled to Russia for a summit with Vladimir Putin, followed by Russian President Putin visiting Pyongyang in June 2024 to sign the landmark Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty pledging mutual military assistance in case of aggression. Domestically, North Korea dismantled the Monument to the Three Charters for National Reunification in Pyongyang after officially declaring South Korea an irreconcilable hostile state, conducted successful launches of the Malligyong-1 military spy satellite, and accelerated construction of 50,000 modern residential flats in Pyongyang.
historicalFigures: Kim Jong Un (President of State Affairs)
ethnicGroups: Korean ~99.8% (one of the world's most ethnically homogeneous societies)
Small Chinese community and tiny resident Japanese diaspora ~0.2%
religions: Officially atheist state; traditional Korean shamanism, Buddhism, and Chondoism (Religion of the Heavenly Way) preserved under state oversight; organized religious activities strictly regulated
education: Kim Il Sung University, Kim Chaek University of Technology (premier engineering institution), and Pyongyang University of Foreign Studies; universal state-funded compulsory 12-year basic and secondary education.
healthcare: Nominally free universal healthcare system under the Ministry of Public Health; village clinics and district polyclinics supported by Traditional Korean Medicine (Koryo medicine) alongside modern pharmaceuticals.
socialCustoms: Immense state loyalty and reverence for the Kim leadership dynasty; wearing leadership badges (Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il lapel pins) over the heart; communal work brigades; Sunday neighborhood clean-up campaigns.
etiquette: Showing paramount respect to leadership portraits and national monuments (bowing before statues at Mansu Hill); bowing slightly to elders and superiors; polite speech registers in Korean.
nationalIdentity: Formed through the Juche ideology of national self-reliance, martial pride in military might and nuclear deterrence, shared Korean cultural roots, and collective unity under the Supreme Leader.
sectors: Industry, Metallurgy & Mining 46%, Services 32%, Agriculture & Fisheries 22%
industries: Military defense equipment, ammunition, and missile assembly
Anthracite coal and mineral mining
Ferrous and non-ferrous metallurgy (steel, iron, lead, zinc)
Chemical manufacturing and synthetic fibers (Vinalon - the "Juche fiber")
Cement and heavy construction
Textile sewing and light consumer manufacturing
agriculture: Rice (irrigated paddy fields in western coastal plains)
naturalResources: Vast coal deposits (anthracite and thermal coal)
Iron ore (Musan iron mine - one of the largest in Asia)
energy: Dominated by coal-fired thermal power and hydroelectric river dams (Supung Dam, Huichon power stations); persistent domestic electricity shortages managed through rolling grid rationing and widespread small rooftop solar PV panels in residential towns
exports: Anthracite coal, iron ore, and minerals (primarily to China under regulatory quotas)
Defense materiel and munitions (to Russia under bilateral strategic treaties)
imports: Crude petroleum and refined fuels (via pipelines from China and rail from Russia)
tradePartners: China (>90% of formal recorded external trade)
Russia (rapidly expanding strategic, logistics, and energy trade post-2023)
tourism: Regulated state tourism operating through Korea International Travel Company (KITC); foreign visitors travel on strictly guided itineraries visiting Pyongyang, the DMZ at Panmunjom, Mount Myohyang, and Kaesong.
employment: Universal state employment allocation in collective farms, state-owned enterprises, armed forces, or municipal construction brigades; informal consumer market trading (Jangmadang).
debtInflation: Dual-currency reality with widespread domestic circulation of Chinese Yuan (RMB) and US Dollars in markets alongside official North Korean Won; state banks promoting electronic electronic card transactions (Narae card).
transport: State railway network (electrified mainline linking Pyongyang to Sinuiju/China, Tumangang/Russia, and coastal industrial zones); Pyongyang Metro (one of the deepest subways in the world, over 100m underground, doubling as a bomb shelter); trolleybuses and trams in Pyongyang.
airports: Pyongyang Sunan International Airport (FNJ - modern terminal hub for state airline Air Koryo)
ports: Port of Nampo (primary western maritime gateway with the massive 8 km West Sea Barrage)
Port of Rason (Rajin - ice-free northeastern port with direct rail to Russia)
Port of Chongjin
Port of Wonsan
internetUsage: <1.0% access to global internet (restricted to top state, scientific, and security leadership); widespread domestic intranet (Kwangmyong) accessible via desktop terminals and domestic smartphones (Pyongyang, Arirang models)
cuisine: Cold Noodles / Pyongyang Naengmyeon (famous national dish: chewy buckwheat noodles served in chilled, tangy beef and pheasant broth with dongchimi radish water, topped with sliced beef, boiled egg, and mustard), Pyongyang Onban (warm rice dish topped with shredded chicken, mung bean pancakes, and mushrooms in savory chicken broth), Kimchi (crisp, refreshing, less spicy northern variety made with cabbage and radishes), Kaesong Pyeonsu (square dumplings filled with vegetables and beef), Taedong River mullet soup (Taedonggang Suno-guk), and sweet Songpyeon rice cakes.
festivals: Day of the Sun (April 15 - Birthday of Kim Il Sung, grandest state holiday)
Day of the Shining Star (February 16 - Birthday of Kim Jong Il)
Day of the Foundation of the Republic (September 9)
Mass Games and artistic performances (Arirang festival legacy)
New Year's Day
music: Massive revolutionary choral and orchestral music (State Merited Chorus, Moranbong Band - all-female electric pop group, Samjiyon Orchestra); folk songs played on the Kayagum and Okryugum (modernized zither created in North Korea); traditional Arirang folk melody.
dance: Mass synchronised dance displays performed in Kim Il Sung Square by thousands of college students in colorful traditional attire; classical Korean fan dance (Buchaechum) and sword dance.
art: Socialist Realism and Chosonhwa (traditional Korean ink wash painting technique adapted with vibrant, realistic oil-like colors depicting revolutionary themes, workers, soldiers, and Mount Paektu); monumental bronze sculpture from the Mansudae Art Studio (one of the largest art production centers in the world).
architecture: Monumental neoclassical and socialist architecture in Pyongyang: Juche Tower (170-meter granite needle crowned by an illuminated red torch), Grand People's Study House, Triumph Arch (larger than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris), Ryugyong Hotel (105-story pyramid skyscraper), and the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun (mausoleum of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il); historic wooden Joseon dynasty gates in Kaesong.
literature: Revolutionary literary fiction and dramatic plays patronized by the state ("The Sea of Blood", "The Flower Girl"); classical Korean poetry and historical chronicles.
cinema: The North Korean film industry produced classics like "The Flower Girl" (1972) and martial arts movie "Hong Kil Dong" (1986); cinematic treatises authored by Kim Jong Il ("On the Art of the Cinema").
sports: Weightlifting (global Olympic powerhouse: multiple Olympic Gold medals and world records won by Om Yun-chol, Rim Jong-sim, and world-record performances in 2024); Women's Football (world champions at youth levels, multi-time AFC Women's Asian Cup champions); Table Tennis (historic mixed doubles Olympic silver medal at Paris 2024); Gymnastics; Taekwondo (ITF - International Taekwon-Do Federation headquarters in Pyongyang).
media: Korean Central News Agency (KCNA - official state news agency), Rodong Sinmun (Newspaper of the Central Committee of the WPK), and Korean Central Television (KCTV).
clothing: Joseon-ot (traditional Korean dress: Chima skirt and Jeogori jacket in vibrant colors worn for state holidays and formal events); functional modern suits, dark coats, and Mao-style tunics (Inminbok) worn by men; military uniforms ubiquitous across all levels of society.
crafts: Traditional Korean mother-of-pearl lacquerware, Koryo celadon ceramics, handwoven silk, and Kaesong Insam (Ginseng) tonics and extracts.
worldHeritageSites: Complex of Koguryo Tombs (famed for exquisite 5th-century colored wall frescoes)
Historic Monuments and Sites in Kaesong (Manwoldae palace, Kaesong Chomsongdae observatory, Sungkyunkwan academy)
unescoIntangible: Arirang folk song in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Tradition of kimchi-making in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
famousPeople: Rim Jong-sim (two-time Olympic weightlifting gold medalist)
Kim Yo Jong (Vice Department Director of WPK)
flagDescription: A horizontal triband of blue (top, symbolizing peace and sovereignty), red (wide central stripe, symbolizing revolutionary spirit and socialist determination), and blue (bottom), separated by narrow white stripes (symbolizing purity and the Korean nation); on the hoist side of the central red stripe is a white circle bearing a red five-pointed star (symbolizing the building of socialism and the Workers' Party).
coatOfArmsDescription: A national emblem depicting a massive hydroelectric power plant beneath the glowing five-pointed red star of socialism, framed by ears of ripe rice tied with a red ribbon bearing the inscription "Democratic People's Republic of Korea" in Chosŏn'gŭl script.

name: Oman
nationalDay: November 18 (National Day - Birthday of late Sultan Qaboos)
motto: None (Unofficial: Peace, Heritage, and Harmony)
coastline: 3,165 km (Arabian Sea, Gulf of Oman, and the strategic Strait of Hormuz at Musandam)
highestPoint: Jabal Shams (Mountain of the Sun, 3,009 m in the Hajar Mountains)
longestRiver: None (no permanent rivers; seasonal flowing wadis: Wadi Shab, Wadi Bani Khalid, Wadi Tiwi)
majorLakes: None (natural coastal lagoons / Khawrs in Dhofar, and mountain wadi pools)
majorMountains: Al Hajar Mountains (Western and Eastern Hajar, dividing coastal Batinah from interior)
climate: Arid desert and subtropical; hot and dry interior; hot and humid coastal plains; Dhofar region in the south experiences the unique summer monsoon (Khareef) from June to September, turning the arid mountains into lush, mist-shrouded green paradises
naturalHazards: Severe tropical cyclones entering the Arabian Sea (e.g., Cyclone Gonu, Cyclone Shaheen)
Flash flooding in narrow rocky mountain wadis
Periodic summer sandstorms
environmentalIssues: Extreme freshwater scarcity requiring seawater desalination
Preservation of fragile coastal mangrove lagoons and coral reefs
Overgrazing and desertification in southern rangelands
biodiversity: Remarkable Arabian biodiversity: Arabian oryx sanctuary (reintroduced into the wild), Arabian leopard (critically endangered in Dhofar's Jabal Samhan), green sea turtle nesting sanctuaries at Ras al Jinz, Arabian humpback whales, and frankincense trees (Boswellia sacra)
languages: English (widely spoken in commerce, business, and tourism)
Balochi, Lawati, and South Arabian indigenous languages (Mehri, Shehri/Jibbali in Dhofar)
currency: Omani Rial (OMR, ر.ع. - 3rd highest-valued currency in the world: pegged at 1 OMR = 2.60 USD)
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Haitham bin Tariq (held by the Sultan)
legislature: Council of Oman (Majlis Oman: appointed State Council / Majlis al-Dawla, and elected Consultative Council / Majlis al-Shura)
constitution: Basic Statute of the State (promulgated in 1996; revised in 2021 to establish a designated Crown Prince)
mainPoliticalParties: Political parties are constitutionally prohibited; citizens elect the 90 members of the Consultative Council via direct universal suffrage
latestElections: Consultative Council (Majlis al-Shura) elections in October 2023 (conducted 100% digitally via the "Intakhib" smartphone app); municipal council elections in 2022
politicalSituation: Under Sultan Haitham bin Tariq (who succeeded the beloved late Sultan Qaboos bin Said in January 2020), Oman is methodically executing its "Oman Vision 2040" transformation. The administration achieved substantial fiscal stabilization, eliminated sovereign budget deficits, reduced public debt, and designated Crown Prince Theyazin bin Haitham. Internationally, Oman remains the universally trusted diplomatic mediator ("Switzerland of the Middle East"), brokering delicate negotiations between Western nations, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and regional factions.
foreignRelations: Founding member of the GCC, Arab League, and UN; renowned for constructive neutrality, independent foreign policy, and backchannel diplomatic mediation (facilitating the 2015 JCPOA Iran nuclear talks and regional hostage releases); strategic defense agreements with the United Kingdom and United States.
military: Sultan of Oman's Armed Forces (Royal Army of Oman, Royal Air Force of Oman with Eurofighter Typhoon and F-16 jets, Royal Navy of Oman commanding the Strait of Hormuz, and Royal Guard of Oman).
adminDivisions: 11 governorates (muhafazat): Muscat, Dhofar, Musandam, Buraimi, Dakhiliyah, Batinah North, Batinah South, Sharqiyah North, Sharqiyah South, Dhahirah, and Wusta
history: Oman was an ancient center of copper mining and maritime trade known to the Sumerians as "Magan" in the 3rd millennium BC. It was also the cradle of the ancient Frankincense Trade, where fragrant resin harvested from Boswellia trees in Dhofar was transported across caravan and sea routes to Rome, Egypt, and India. Oman was one of the earliest lands to embrace Islam peacefully in 630 AD during the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad. The Ibadi school of Islam established an elective Imamate in the interior mountains in the 8th century, which coexisted with maritime sultanates on the coast. In 1507, Portuguese explorer Afonso de Albuquerque conquered Muscat and coastal ports, fortifying them with forts Al Jalali and Al Mirani. The Yaruba Dynasty expelled the Portuguese in 1650, building a formidable maritime empire. In 1744, Ahmad bin Said al-Busaidi founded the current Al Said Dynasty. In the 19th century, under Sultan Said bin Sultan, the Omani Empire reached its zenith, controlling Zanzibar, parts of the East African coast, and Gwadar (in modern Pakistan), making Zanzibar the co-capital of the empire. Following his death, the realm was divided into the Sultanate of Zanzibar and the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman. Sultan Qaboos bin Said overthrew his father in 1970, launching the "Omani Renaissance", uniting the country, ending the Dhofar rebellion, and transforming an impoverished state with only 10 km of paved roads into a modern, prosperous nation while preserving traditional Arabian architecture and cultural heritage.
recentEvents2020_2026: Sultan Qaboos passed away peacefully in January 2020 after 50 years of visionary rule, succeeded smoothly by his cousin Sultan Haitham bin Tariq. Sultan Haitham reformed governance under Royal Decree 6/2021, creating the formal role of Crown Prince (conferred on his son Sayyid Theyazin bin Haitham). Between 2022 and 2026, Oman turned sovereign debt into investment-grade fiscal surpluses, developed the multi-billion-dollar Special Economic Zone at Duqm (including the modern Duqm Refinery), signed landmark green hydrogen and ammonia export agreements through "Hydrom" attracting >$30 billion in international commitments, and served as chief mediator in ceasefire and humanitarian talks for Yemen.
historicalFigures: Sultan Qaboos bin Said (Architect of Modern Oman)
Ahmad bin Said al-Busaidi (Founder of Al Said Dynasty)
Said bin Sultan (Ruler of Omani-Zanzibar Empire)
Ahmad ibn Majid (legendary 15th-century Omani navigator and cartographer)
ethnicGroups: Omani citizens ~58% (Arab heritage, with historical Swahili, Balochi, and Lawati communities reflecting maritime empire roots)
Expatriate residents ~42% (predominantly Indian, Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Egyptian, and Filipino professionals)
religions: Islam ~85.9% (predominantly Ibadi Islam ~45%, Sunni ~45%, Shia ~5%; renowned for exemplary sectarian tolerance and peaceful coexistence)
education: Sultan Qaboos University (SQU in Al Khoudh - premier national research university), University of Nizwa, and German University of Technology in Oman (GUtech); primary and secondary education free for all Omani citizens.
healthcare: Comprehensive universal healthcare provided by the Ministry of Health through modern regional hospitals (Royal Hospital and Khoula Hospital in Muscat, Sultan Qaboos Hospital in Salalah); recognized by the WHO for world-leading efficiency in health service delivery.
socialCustoms: Coffee and dates hospitality: serving Omani Kahwa (coffee flavored with cardamom and saffron) accompanied by fresh dates and Halwa; wearing national dress with pride; gathering at the Sablah (communal village council hall) for weddings, funerals, and social discussions.
etiquette: Warm handshakes; accepting coffee and dates with the right hand; shaking the small cup gently from side to side when finished; conservative modesty in public spaces; high respect for elders and royal decrees.
nationalIdentity: Deeply anchored in maritime seafaring heritage, ancient frankincense trade legacy, peaceful and tolerant Ibadi Islamic values, unique architectural aesthetics avoiding garish skyscrapers, and national pride in modernization without losing cultural soul.
sectors: Oil & Hydrocarbons 33%, Services & Logistics 50%, Manufacturing & Mining 15%, Agriculture & Fisheries 2%
industries: Crude petroleum and natural gas extraction (Petroleum Development Oman - PDO)
Liquefied natural gas (Oman LNG in Sur)
Petroleum refining and petrochemicals (OQ: Duqm Refinery, Sohar Refinery)
Green hydrogen and ammonia development (Hydrom)
Port logistics and maritime transshipment (Salalah, Sohar, Duqm)
Aluminum smelting (Sohar Aluminium)
Mining (limestone, gypsum, copper)
agriculture: Dates (over 8 million date palms producing premium Fardh and Khalas varieties)
Pomegranates, walnuts, and roses (Jabal Akhdar mountain terraces)
naturalResources: Natural gas deposits (Khazzan tight gas mega-field)
World-class solar and wind energy resources (among the highest photovoltaic irradiance globally)
energy: Dominated by natural gas; executing an aggressive green hydrogen roadmap targeting 1 million tonnes of green hydrogen annually by 2030 through massive wind and solar concessions in Duqm and Dhofar; operational Ibri II 500 MW solar park and Amin solar park
imports: Transport motor vehicles and spare parts
tradePartners: China (largest crude oil buyer, purchasing >80% of Omani oil exports)
India (major bilateral trade and investment partner)
tourism: Surpassed 4.2 million international tourists drawn to Muscat's white architecture and Royal Opera House, historic mud-brick forts of Nizwa and Bahla, wadi canyoning in Wadi Shab and Bimmah Sinkhole, turtle watching at Ras al Jinz, dramatic fjords of Musandam ("Norway of Arabia"), and the lush green summer Khareef season in Salalah.
employment: Omanization policy systematically increasing citizen participation in the private workforce; expanding private banking, fintech, renewable engineering, and tourism sectors; low unemployment among citizens (~3.8%).
debtInflation: Strong sovereign balance sheet; public debt declined to ~35% of GDP; sovereign wealth assets managed by Oman Investment Authority (OIA) exceeding $50 billion; inflation maintained low at ~1.5%.
transport: Oman-Etihad Rail (Hafeet Rail connecting Sohar Port to Abu Dhabi via high-speed freight and passenger rail); modern 8-lane expressways (Muscat Expressway, Batinah Expressway); state-of-the-art Muscat International Airport; passenger and vehicle catamarans operated by National Ferries Company.
airports: Muscat International Airport (MCT - award-winning modern terminal designed for 20M passengers, hub of Oman Air)
ports: Port of Salalah (world-class transshipment container hub on the Indian Ocean)
Port of Sohar (deepwater industrial and bulk container port)
Port of Duqm (mega multi-purpose port, drydock, and naval facility)
Port Sultan Qaboos (cruise and maritime tourism hub in Muscat)
cuisine: Shuwa (legendary national culinary masterpiece: bone-in lamb or goat marinated in a rich, fiery paste of dates, coriander, cumin, red chili, and vinegar, wrapped in banana or palm leaves, placed inside a woven palm-frond sack, and slow-roasted for 24 to 48 hours in a communal underground sand pit oven, served at Eid over fragrant spiced saffron rice), Majboos / Kabsa (fragrant rice cooked with meat and dried black lime), Mashuai (spit-roasted kingfish served with lemon rice), Harees (slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge), and Omani Halwa (world-famous sweet delicacy made from starch, caramelized sugar, clarified butter / Ghee, saffron, cardamom, and rosewater, topped with toasted almonds and cashews, served hot with bitter black cardamom coffee).
festivals: National Day (November 18)
Salalah Tourism Festival (celebrating the misty green Khareef season from July to August with music and cultural events)
Muscat Festival (annual cultural arts and heritage festival)
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha (marked by communal Shuwa feasts)
Tour of Oman (professional cycling race)
music: Traditional Omani music incorporating Arabian, East African, and Persian musical influences; Razha (traditional musical poetry duel accompanied by sword tossing); Oud playing; world-class classical symphony orchestra (Royal Oman Symphony Orchestra - ROSO, founded by Sultan Qaboos).
dance: Razha and Ayyala sword dances (performed by men in rows reciting poetry and Brandishing swords); Liwa and Dan (vibrant drumming dances reflecting East African seafaring heritage); Dhofari female folk dances.
art: Bait Al Zubair and National Museum of Oman; exquisite Islamic calligraphy, silver dagger craftsmanship, contemporary Omani fine art at the Omani Society for Fine Arts.
architecture: Strict municipal building codes preserving authentic Omani white and cream Islamic architecture with arched windows, crenellated rooflines, and carved wooden doors (skyscrapers are prohibited in Muscat); Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque (monumental white marble mosque featuring a 50m golden dome, 8.5-ton Swarovski crystal chandelier, and a handwoven Persian carpet); Royal Opera House Muscat (stunning marble and teakwood cultural palace); UNESCO mud-brick fortress of Bahla Fort and Nizwa Fort with its massive round tower.
literature: Centuries of Islamic scholarship and navigational literature (Ahmad ibn Majid's nautical treatises); modern Omani literature: Jokha Alharthi (author of "Celestial Bodies", first Arabic-language novel to win the prestigious International Booker Prize in 2019); poetry of Saif Ghobash.
cinema: Emerging cinema scene supported by the Muscat International Film Festival and Oman Film and Theatre Society; international filming location for desert and maritime features.
sports: Football (Oman won the Arabian Gulf Cup in 2009 and 2017; legendary goalkeeper Ali Al-Habsi played in the English Premier League); Camel Racing (prestigious traditional races with robotic jockeys); Traditional Dhow Sailing and modern oceanic sailing (Oman Sail); Horse Riding and Showjumping.
media: Oman News Agency (ONA), Oman Daily Observer (English daily), Times of Oman, Oman Daily (Arabic), and Oman TV.
clothing: Men wear the Dishdasha (collarless white or muted pastel robe featuring a delicate short tassel called Farakha / Tarboosha lightly scented with perfume) paired with the embroidered Kumma round cap or Mussar wool turban, and for formal events the ceremonial silver Khanjar (curved dagger) tucked into an embroidered belt; women wear vibrant embroidered tunics with matching trousers (Sirwal) and Shayla headscarf, or elegant black Abayas.
crafts: Omani Khanjar silversmithing (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Bahla traditional pottery (UNESCO), copper coffeepot making (Dallah), rosewater distillation on Jabal Akhdar, and palm-leaf weaving.
worldHeritageSites: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
Land of Frankincense (Wadi Dawkah, Shisr/Ubar, Sumhuram, Al-Baleed)
Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman (ancient 2,000-year-old gravity water channels)
unescoIntangible: Al-Khanjar, craft skills and social practices
Date palm, knowledge, skills, traditions and practices
flagDescription: A horizontal tricolor of white (top, symbolizing peace and prosperity), red (middle, the historical color of the flag, representing battles fought against foreign invaders), and green (bottom, fertility and the Green Mountain / Jabal Akhdar), with a vertical red stripe at the hoist bearing the national emblem of Oman (the Khanjar and crossed swords) in white in the canton.
coatOfArmsDescription: The national emblem consists of an Omani Khanjar (curved dagger) in an ornate sheath, superimposed on two crossed scimitars / broadswords linked by a ceremonial belt, symbolizing historic defense, honor, and royal authority.
landmarks: Bimmah Sinkhole and Wadi Shab (emerald water canyon)
Jabal Shams (the Grand Canyon of Arabia)
Land of Frankincense sites and Salalah coastal Khareef
travelNotes: Extremely safe, welcoming, and pristine country; ranked among the most peaceful nations globally; e-Visas readily obtainable online via the Royal Oman Police portal; rental cars are ideal for exploring mountain wadis and desert dunes; modest dress is appreciated in towns and required in religious monuments; tap water is treated and drinkable in Muscat.
shortSummary: Oman is an enchanting Arabian sultanate where ancient frankincense trade heritage, historic mud-brick mountain forts, and dramatic desert canyons meet the sparkling Arabian Sea, governed by enlightened leadership, legendary hospitality, and constructive global diplomacy.
geography: Spanning 309,500 km² across Western Asia / Arabian Peninsula. Highest point: Jabal Shams (Mountain of the Sun, 3,009 m in the Hajar Mountains); lowest point: Arabian Sea (0 m). Longest river: None (no permanent rivers; seasonal flowing wadis: Wadi Shab, Wadi Bani Khalid, Wadi Tiwi). Climate: Arid desert and subtropical; hot and dry interior; hot and humid coastal plains; Dhofar region in the south experiences the unique summer monsoon (Khareef) from June to September, turning the arid mountains into lush, mist-shrouded green paradises.
economy: Economy with GDP nominal of $115 billion (approx. 2026) ($24,200 per capita). Leading sectors: Oil & Hydrocarbons 33%, Services & Logistics 50%, Manufacturing & Mining 15%, Agriculture & Fisheries 2%. Main industries: Crude petroleum and natural gas extraction (Petroleum Development Oman - PDO), Liquefied natural gas (Oman LNG in Sur), Petroleum refining and petrochemicals (OQ: Duqm Refinery, Sohar Refinery), Green hydrogen and ammonia development (Hydrom), Port logistics and maritime transshipment (Salalah, Sohar, Duqm), Aluminum smelting (Sohar Aluminium), Mining (limestone, gypsum, copper). Key exports: Crude petroleum, Liquefied natural gas (LNG), Refined petroleum fuels and polypropylene, Chemical fertilizers (urea, ammonia), Raw aluminum, Gypsum and minerals, Fresh fish and seafood.
culture: Rich cultural traditions featuring cuisine (Shuwa (legendary national culinary masterpiece: bone-in lamb or goat marinated in a rich, fiery paste of dates, coriander, cumin, red chili, and vinegar, wrapped in banana or palm leaves, placed inside a woven palm-frond sack, and slow-roasted for 24 to 48 hours in a communal underground sand pit oven, served at Eid over fragrant spiced saffron rice), Majboos / Kabsa (fragrant rice cooked with meat and dried black lime), Mashuai (spit-roasted kingfish served with lemon rice), Harees (slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge), and Omani Halwa (world-famous sweet delicacy made from starch, caramelized sugar, clarified butter / Ghee, saffron, cardamom, and rosewater, topped with toasted almonds and cashews, served hot with bitter black cardamom coffee).), traditional music and dance (Traditional Omani music incorporating Arabian, East African, and Persian musical influences; Razha (traditional musical poetry duel accompanied by sword tossing); Oud playing; world-class classical symphony orchestra (Royal Oman Symphony Orchestra - ROSO, founded by Sultan Qaboos).; Razha and Ayyala sword dances (performed by men in rows reciting poetry and Brandishing swords); Liwa and Dan (vibrant drumming dances reflecting East African seafaring heritage); Dhofari female folk dances.), literature (Centuries of Islamic scholarship and navigational literature (Ahmad ibn Majid's nautical treatises); modern Omani literature: Jokha Alharthi (author of "Celestial Bodies", first Arabic-language novel to win the prestigious International Booker Prize in 2019); poetry of Saif Ghobash.), and sports (Football (Oman won the Arabian Gulf Cup in 2009 and 2017; legendary goalkeeper Ali Al-Habsi played in the English Premier League); Camel Racing (prestigious traditional races with robotic jockeys); Traditional Dhow Sailing and modern oceanic sailing (Oman Sail); Horse Riding and Showjumping.).

name: Pakistan
largestCity: Karachi (megacity and financial hub on the Arabian Sea)
nationalDay: March 23 (Pakistan Day / Republic Day - Lahore Resolution in 1940) / August 14 (Independence Day in 1947)
motto: Faith, Unity, Discipline (ایمان، اتحاد، نظم - Īmān, Ittiḥād, Nazm)
coastline: 1,046 km (Arabian Sea and Gulf of Oman coastline)
highestPoint: K2 / Mount Godwin-Austen (8,611 m in the Karakoram Range - second highest peak on Earth)
longestRiver: Indus River (Sindhu, 3,180 km - lifeblood river basin flowing north to south)
majorLakes: Manchar Lake (largest freshwater lake in Pakistan)
Attabad Lake (formed in 2010 landslide in Hunza)
majorMountains: Karakoram Range (dense concentration of 8,000m peaks: K2, Gasherbrum I & II, Broad Peak)
climate: Diverse across dramatic elevations: arid to hyper-arid desert in Balochistan, hot semi-arid plains in Punjab and Sindh with intense summer heat exceeding 48°C, monsoon rains from July to September, and polar-alpine glacial freeze in northern mountains
naturalHazards: Severe catastrophic monsoon flooding (e.g., 2022 historic floods submerging one-third of the country)
Destructive earthquakes along the boundary of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates
Severe heatwaves and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs)
environmentalIssues: Extreme vulnerability to global climate change impact
Smog and particulate air pollution crisis in Lahore and Punjab during autumn/winter crop burning
Water stress and siltation of major irrigation dams (Tarbela, Mangla)
Deforestation
biodiversity: Astonishing transition from mangroves to mountain glaciers: markhor (flare-horned wild mountain goat, national animal), snow leopard, Indus river dolphin (endangered blind dolphin / Bhulan), Asiatic black bear, blue sheep, and marine turtle nesting in Balochistan
languages: English (official language of law, executive government, and higher education)
legislature: Parliament of Pakistan (Majlis-e-Shoora: Senate and National Assembly)
constitution: Adopted in 1973; enshrines federal parliamentary system and Islamic legal character
mainPoliticalParties: Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N - governing coalition lead)
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI - led by imprisoned former PM Imran Khan, independent candidates)
latestElections: 12th National Assembly general election in February 2024; Shehbaz Sharif sworn in as Prime Minister heading a coalition; Asif Ali Zardari elected President in March 2024
politicalSituation: Under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari, Pakistan is implementing a rigorous 37-month $7 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility program to stabilize external balances, restore foreign exchange reserves, and tame inflation. The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) is driving foreign investment from GCC partners (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar) and China into mining (Reko Diq copper-gold project), energy, and agriculture, while managing domestic political tensions and cross-border security challenges along the Afghan and Iranian borders.
foreignRelations: All-weather strategic cooperative partnership with China (central anchor of the $65 billion China-Pakistan Economic Corridor / CPEC); close defense and economic ties with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Turkey; nuclear-armed state; non-NATO ally status with the US; historically contested relations with India over the Kashmir dispute.
military: Pakistan Armed Forces (Pakistan Army, Pakistan Navy, Pakistan Air Force; 6th largest standing military globally; nuclear-armed with comprehensive multi-range ballistic, cruise, and tactical missile defense triad).
adminDivisions: 4 provinces (Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan), 1 federal capital territory (Islamabad Capital Territory), and 2 autonomous administrative territories (Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan)
history: Pakistan is home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (c. 3300–1300 BC), centered at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, pioneering urban drainage, brick architecture, and standardized weights. Gandhara blossomed as a global hub of Greco-Buddhist art in Taxila (conquered by Alexander the Great in 326 BC) under the Kushan Empire. Muhammad bin Qasim introduced Islam to Sindh ("Bab-ul-Islam" / Gateway of Islam) in 711 AD. The region flourished under the Delhi Sultanate and reached an artistic, imperial peak under the Mughal Empire, with Lahore serving as imperial capital under Akbar and Jahangir (constructing the Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort, and Shalimar Gardens). Following the fall of the Sikh Empire in 1849, the British Raj annexed the territory. The Pakistan Movement, conceptualized by philosopher-poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal in 1930 and championed by Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam / Great Leader) through the All-India Muslim League, secured the creation of Pakistan as an independent homeland for Muslims on August 14, 1947, through the Partition of British India. Originally consisting of West and East Pakistan, the eastern wing seceded in 1971 following a tragic civil war to become Bangladesh. Under Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Pakistan adopted its 1973 democratic constitution and initiated its nuclear program, successfully conducting nuclear tests in 1998 (Youm-e-Takbeer). Modern political history has cycled between democratic civilian administrations and military governments (Ayub Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, Pervez Musharraf).
recentEvents2020_2026: Catastrophic monsoon floods in summer 2022 affected over 33 million citizens and caused over $30 billion in damages, sparking global climate justice mobilization at COP27. In February 2024, Pakistan held highly competitive general elections leading to a coalition government headed by Shehbaz Sharif. Between 2024 and 2026, Pakistan secured a critical $7 billion IMF stabilization package, advanced commercial development of the monumental Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan with Barrick Gold, inaugurated the upgraded Gwadar International Airport under CPEC, and celebrated national pride in Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem.
historicalFigures: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam - Father of the Nation)
Fatima Jinnah (Madar-e-Millat / Mother of the Nation)
Benazir Bhutto (first female prime minister of a Muslim-majority nation)
ethnicGroups: Kashmiri, Brahui, Hindkowan, Balti, Shina, and Hazara ~3.9%
religions: Sikhism, Ahmadiyya, Zoroastrian (Parsi), and Kalash indigenous animists ~0.1%
literacyRate: 59.1% (youth literacy exceeds 72%; substantial urban-rural and gender disparities)
education: Historic institutions include University of the Punjab (Lahore, founded 1882), Quaid-i-Azam University (Islamabad), National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Aga Khan University, and Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS); producing tens of thousands of software engineers and medical doctors annually.
healthcare: Tertiary healthcare centered in major teaching hospitals: Mayo Hospital, Jinnah Post Graduate Medical Centre (JPMC Karachi), and Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital; Sehat Sahulat universal health insurance card program providing subsidized inpatient treatment in KP and Punjab.
socialCustoms: Profound hospitality (Mehmaan Nawazi); Pashtunwali code in northwestern hills; vibrant multi-day weddings (Mehndi, Barat, Walima) filled with Dholak drumming and Bhangra dancing; gathering for late-night chai at Dhabas; Sufi shrine pilgrimages (Urs).
etiquette: Warm handshakes with "As-salamu alaykum", often followed by a gentle embrace (Mu'anaqa) between men; conservative modesty in dress; elders are served first at meals; using the right hand for eating and exchange of gifts.
nationalIdentity: United under Islamic ideological founding, the Urdu language, shared passion for cricket, reverence for Jinnah and Iqbal, rich regional ethnic traditions, and resilience in overcoming environmental and economic adversity.
sectors: Services 54%, Agriculture 23%, Industry & Manufacturing 23%
industries: Textiles and apparel manufacturing (spinning, weaving, knitwear, denim - world's 4th largest cotton producer and major exporter)
Pharmaceuticals and surgical instruments (Sialkot supplies over 70% of global hand-held surgical instruments)
Sports goods manufacturing (Sialkot hand-stitches the official FIFA World Cup match balls)
Information technology and freelance software engineering (3rd largest global freelance provider)
Cement, steel, and fertilizers (Fauji Fertilizer, Engro)
Automotive and motorcycle assembly
agriculture: Mangoes (world-famous Chaunsa, Sindhri varieties) and citrus (Kinnow)
naturalResources: Copper and gold reserves (Reko Diq, Saindak in Balochistan - one of the world's largest untapped deposits)
Coal (Thar coalfield - over 175 billion tonnes of lignite)
Rock salt (Khewra Salt Mine - source of authentic pink Himalayan salt)
energy: Diverse energy mix: expanding Thar coal power projects; major hydroelectric dams (Tarbela, Mangla, and under-construction Diamer-Bhasha and Mohmand dams); operating 6 nuclear power reactors (Chashma and KANUPP Karachi built with CNNC); expanding solar PV
exports: Textiles, knitwear, bedwear, and cotton yarn
Sports goods and leather apparel (FIFA match balls)
tradePartners: United States (largest single export destination for textiles)
China (largest total trade partner and import source)
European Union (notably Germany, UK, Netherlands under GSP+)
tourism: Surpassed 2.5 million international and domestic tourists drawn to northern mountain trekking in Gilgit-Baltistan (Karakoram Highway, Hunza Valley, Skardu, Fairy Meadows, K2 Base Camp), historical Mughal monuments of Lahore, ancient Mohenjo-daro and Taxila ruins, and pristine beaches of Gwadar.
employment: Agriculture employs ~38% of the workforce; booming digital IT freelance economy; over 9 million overseas Pakistanis sending over $30 billion in annual remittances.
debtInflation: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) maintains high benchmark interest rates to anchor disinflation; foreign exchange reserves rebuilt to >$11 billion; inflation decelerating toward single digits (~9-10%).
transport: Karakoram Highway (KKH - 8th Wonder of the World, connecting Pakistan with China across the 4,693 m Khunjerab Pass); Motorway network (M-2 Lahore-Islamabad, M-5 Multan-Sukkur); Pakistan Railways mainline; Gwadar Deep Sea Port; Lahore Orange Line Metro (Pakistan's first automated rapid transit line).
ports: Port of Karachi (historic primary commercial seaport)
Port Muhammad Bin Qasim (major industrial bulk and container port)
Gwadar Port (deepwater warm-water hub at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, centerpiece of CPEC)
internetUsage: 43.5% (rapid expansion of 4G/5G mobile broadband, over 190 million cellular subscriptions, and universal digital mobile wallets: Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast instant payment system)
cuisine: Renowned for rich Mughlai, Punjabi, Sindhi, and Pashtun culinary mastery: Biryani (Karachi spicy layered beef or chicken rice with dried plums / Aloo Bukhara and potatoes), Nihari (slow-cooked beef shank stew in bone marrow gravy garnished with ginger slivers, green chilies, and lemon juice, traditionally eaten for breakfast), Karahi (chicken or mutton stir-fried in an iron wok with fresh tomatoes, ginger, and green chilies), Chapli Kebab (large flat minced beef patties spiced with crushed coriander, pomegranate seeds, and tomatoes from Peshawar), Haleem (slow-simmered savory porridge of shredded beef, lentils, and wheat), Sajji (Balochi skewered whole lamb or chicken roasted over open coals stuffed with spiced rice), Seekh Kebabs, and decadent sweets like Gulab Jamun, Jalebi, and Kulfi Falooda.
festivals: Pakistan Day (March 23 - grand military parade in Islamabad)
Independence Day (August 14 - illuminated green-and-white cities and flag hoisting)
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
Shandur Polo Festival (held on the world's highest polo ground at 3,700 m in July)
Sufi Urs festivals (Data Ganj Bakhsh in Lahore, Lal Shahbaz Qalandar in Sehwan)
Basant (historic spring kite festival)
music: Qawwali (ecstatic Sufi devotional music pioneered globally by Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, Rahat Fateh Ali Khan, and the Sabri Brothers); Ghazal singing (Mehdi Hassan, Ghulam Ali, Iqbal Bano); Coke Studio Pakistan (world-renowned music television platform blending indigenous folk, Sufi, and contemporary fusion, producing global hits like "Pasoori"); Rubab and Dholak folk rhythms.
dance: Bhangra and Luddi (Punjab); Attan (energetic Pashtun warrior circle dance performed with swirling head motions); Khattak sword dance; Lewa (Balochistan); Jhumar.
art: Truck Art (world-famous folk art movement: commercial Bedford trucks decorated with kaleidoscopic hand-painted landscapes, poetry, reflective stickers, and chiming brass chains); Chughtai miniature painting; calligraphy (Sadequain, master calligrapher and modernist muralist); contemporary visual arts (Shahzia Sikander, Rashid Rana).
architecture: Monumental Mughal architecture: Badshahi Mosque (one of the largest mosques in the world), Lahore Fort (UNESCO), and Wazir Khan Mosque (dazzling Persian glazed tile work / Kashi Kari); ancient ruins of Mohenjo-daro and Taxila; modern icons like Faisal Mosque in Islamabad (designed by Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay, resembling a Bedouin tent) and Minar-e-Pakistan.
literature: Allama Muhammad Iqbal (philosophical Urdu and Persian poetry: "Bang-e-Dra", "Asrar-e-Khudi"); Faiz Ahmad Faiz (revolutionary Marxist romantic poet); Saadat Hasan Manto (master short story writer on Partition); modern English novelists: Mohsin Hamid ("The Reluctant Fundamentalist"), Kamila Shamsie, and Bapsi Sidhwa.
cinema: Revitalized Pakistani cinema ("Revival of Lollywood"): international hits and Cannes winners ("Joyland" by Saim Sadiq), record-breaking blockbusters ("The Legend of Maula Jatt", highest-grossing Pakistani film in history); world-renowned television drama serial production (HUM TV, ARY Digital).
sports: Cricket is an overwhelming national obsession (Pakistan won the 1992 Cricket World Cup under Imran Khan, 2009 T20 World Cup, and 2017 Champions Trophy; stars Babar Azam, Shaheen Shah Afridi; Pakistan Super League - PSL); Javelin (Arshad Nadeem won Olympic Gold at Paris 2024 with a historic Olympic record throw of 92.97 m); Field Hockey (four-time World Cup champions and three-time Olympic gold medalists); Squash (unmatched global dynasty: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches; Jansher Khan won eight World Opens); Polo (Shandur).
media: Dawn (historic English daily founded by Jinnah), The News International, Daily Jang (largest Urdu daily), Geo News, ARY News, Dunya News, and PTV (State Broadcaster).
clothing: Shalwar Kameez (national dress worn universally by both men and women across all four provinces: loose tunic and baggy drawstring trousers); women wear the matching Dupatta scarf; men wear the tailored Achkan or Sherwani for weddings and official state functions, paired with Karakul or Pakol caps.
crafts: Sialkot leather and sports goods, Multan blue pottery (Kashigari), Hala glazed ceramics, Chiniot carved rosewood furniture, Peshawari Chappal leather sandals, and handwoven Pashmina and wool carpets.

Fort and Shalamar Gardens in Lahore

name: Palestine
status: UN Non-Member Observer State (recognized by >145 UN member states)
nationalDay: November 15 (Declaration of Independence in 1988) / January 1 (Revolution Day)
motto: None (Unofficial: Freedom, Independence, and Justice)
borders: Jordan (West Bank borders the Jordan River and Dead Sea)
coastline: 40 km (Gaza Strip Mediterranean coastline)
highestPoint: Mount Nabi Yunis in the West Bank (1,030 m in Halhul, Hebron Governorate)
lowestPoint: Dead Sea (-438 m below sea level - lowest dry land point on Earth)
longestRiver: Jordan River (defining the eastern border of the West Bank with Jordan) / Wadi al-Far'a and Wadi Gaza
majorLakes: Dead Sea (hypersaline terminal lake bordering the West Bank)
majorMountains: Samarian Hills (Mount Gerizim, Mount Ebal in Nablus)
climate: Mediterranean; hot, dry summers and cool, rainy winters in the hill country of the West Bank; semi-arid coastal in the Gaza Strip; arid subtropical in the Jordan Valley (Jericho)
naturalHazards: Earthquakes along the Jordan Rift Valley fault line
Severe summer heatwaves and droughts
Winter flash floods in desert wadis and coastal drainage basins
environmentalIssues: Severe freshwater aquifer contamination and scarcity (especially coastal aquifer in Gaza)
Untreated sewage disposal and infrastructure destruction
Uprooting of ancient olive groves and land fragmentation
Solid waste management
biodiversity: Crucial flyway for migrating birds between Europe and Africa: Palestine sunbird (Cinnyris osea - national bird), mountain gazelles in the West Bank hills, caracals, striped hyenas, and ancient olive tree groves (some over 2,000 years old)
languages: English (widely spoken in commerce, administration, and higher education)
Hebrew (understood by many commercial traders and workers)
currency: No national currency; operates on Israeli New Shekel (ILS, ₪), Jordanian Dinar (JOD) in the West Bank, and US Dollars
government: Semi-presidential republic / Palestinian National Authority (PNA) governance facing deep territorial fragmentation
legislature: Palestinian Legislative Council (PLC - suspended; authority exercised by presidential decrees); Palestinian National Council (PNC / PLO)
constitution: Palestinian Basic Law (promulgated in 2002, amended in 2003 and 2005)
mainPoliticalParties: Hamas (Islamic Resistance Movement - de facto authority in Gaza Strip prior to 2023–2024 conflict)
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP)
Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP)
latestElections: Presidential election in 2005; legislative election in 2006; subsequent national general elections postponed due to political division and dispute over voting in East Jerusalem
politicalSituation: In March 2024, President Mahmoud Abbas appointed veteran international economist Dr. Mohammad Mustafa as Prime Minister to lead a technocratic reform cabinet tasked with institutional governance reforms, financial stabilization, and leading monumental post-war recovery and reconstruction planning for the devastated Gaza Strip following the catastrophic 2023–2024 Israel-Hamas war. Palestine expanded formal diplomatic recognition to over 145 sovereign nations (including newly recognized Western European states Spain, Ireland, Norway, and Slovenia in mid-2024) and secured upgraded participatory privileges at the United Nations General Assembly.
foreignRelations: UN Non-Member Observer State; recognized bilaterally by over 145 UN member countries; member of the Arab League, OIC, and Non-Aligned Movement; represented internationally by the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO); receives extensive humanitarian support from the European Union, UNRWA, Arab Gulf states, and international agencies.
military: Palestinian National Security Forces (PNSF: civilian law enforcement, Presidential Guard, and Civil Police in the West Bank; no standing army under Oslo Accords frameworks; various armed factions operate outside official PNA command).

history: Palestine possesses an unbroken multi-millennial history as a crossroads of civilizations. Jericho (Tell es-Sultan) is recognized as the oldest continuously inhabited walled city on Earth, dating back over 11,000 years (Neolithic era). The Canaanites established city-states in the 3rd millennium BC, followed by the Philistines along the southern coast. The land holds supreme spiritual sanctity in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam: Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem and preached throughout the region; for Muslims, Jerusalem (Al-Quds) is the first Qibla and third holiest city, where the Prophet Muhammad ascended to heaven during the Isra and Mi'raj from the Al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock. Ruled successively by ancient Israelites, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Romans, and Byzantines, the territory came under Islamic rule in 637 AD when Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab entered Jerusalem, issuing the peaceful Assurance of Umar. The Crusader period (1099–1187) ended when Saladin (Salah ad-Din) recaptured Jerusalem. Centuries of Mamluk and Ottoman rule (1516–1917) integrated Palestine into regional trade, famed for olive oil, Nabulsi soap, and citrus exports. Following World War I, Britain governed under the League of Nations Mandate for Palestine. The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181 in 1947 proposing partition, followed by the 1948 war and the "Nakba" (Catastrophe), in which over 700,000 Palestinians were displaced from their homes, becoming refugees. In 1967 (the Six-Day War), Israel occupied the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip. The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) under Yasser Arafat was recognized as the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people in 1974. The First Intifada (1987) led to the 1993 Oslo Accords, establishing the Palestinian National Authority with interim autonomy. The failure of final status talks led to the Second Intifada (2000–2005). In 2012, the UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly to grant Palestine Non-Member Observer State status.
recentEvents2020_2026: The October 7, 2023 attacks and the resulting catastrophic war in the Gaza Strip caused unprecedented civilian devastation, displacing over 1.9 million Palestinians, leveling over 60% of Gaza's housing infrastructure, and killing over 43,000 people according to local health authorities. In 2024, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) issued landmark advisory opinions regarding the illegality of the occupation, and the International Criminal Court (ICC) sought arrest warrants. In spring 2024, Spain, Ireland, Norway, and Slovenia officially recognized the State of Palestine, elevating global diplomatic recognition above 145 countries. Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa enacted public sector anti-corruption and fiscal transparency measures to prepare for unified governance across the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

politicalSituation: Under President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. (elected in 2022 alongside Vice President Sara Duterte), the Philippines pursues its "Build Better More" (BBM) infrastructure agenda, implementing nationwide railway, airport, and bridge networks. In foreign policy, Marcos has strategically realigned the Philippines with traditional ally the United States, expanding the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), upgrading naval and air capabilities, asserting sovereign maritime rights in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) within its Exclusive Economic Zone, and maintaining robust commercial ties with Japan and regional partners.
foreignRelations: Founding member of ASEAN; major non-NATO ally of the United States; security partnerships with Japan (Reciprocal Access Agreement signed in 2024), Australia, and South Korea; active proponent of international law and the 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Tribunal ruling under UNCLOS.

history: Inhabited for over 50,000 years (Tabon Man), the islands were settled by Austronesian navigators who built coastal trading polities (Barangays) led by Datus, Rajahs, and Sultans (such as the Sultanate of Sulu and Rajahnate of Cebu) trading gold, pearls, and porcelain with China and Southeast Asia. In 1521, Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan arrived in Cebu, claiming the islands for Spain before being killed by chieftain Lapu-Lapu at the Battle of Mactan. In 1565, Miguel López de Legazpi founded the first Spanish settlement in Cebu, later establishing Manila in 1571. Spain ruled the archipelago for over 330 years, naming it Las Islas Filipinas after King Philip II, introducing Roman Catholicism, and inaugurating the trans-Pacific Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade (1565–1815) exchanging Mexican silver for Chinese silks and spices. In the late 19th century, the Propaganda Movement led by national hero Dr. José Rizal ("Noli Me Tángere") sparked the Philippine Revolution led by Andrés Bonifacio (Katipunan) and Emilio Aguinaldo, who declared Philippine independence on June 12, 1898. Following the Spanish-American War, Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States under the Treaty of Paris. The fierce Philippine-American War (1899–1902) ensued, followed by American civil governance, public English education (the Thomasites), and the 1935 Commonwealth. During World War II, the islands suffered brutal Japanese occupation, the Bataan Death March, and the catastrophic Battle of Manila in 1945. The United States recognized full Philippine independence on July 4, 1946. Ferdinand Marcos ruled from 1965 to 1986, declaring Martial Law in 1972, until ousted by the historic non-violent EDSA People Power Revolution that restored democracy under Corazon Aquino.
recentEvents2020_2026: The Philippines achieved strong post-pandemic economic growth exceeding 6% annually, driven by domestic consumption, digital fintech (GCash), and business process outsourcing (BPO). Ferdinand Marcos Jr. won a landslide presidential victory in May 2022. Between 2023 and 2026, the Philippines signed a landmark Reciprocal Access Agreement (RAA) defense pact with Japan, held trilateral security summits in Washington with the US and Japan, asserted sovereign access to Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin Shoal) in the West Philippine Sea, established the Maharlika Investment Fund (sovereign wealth fund), and made major progress on the Metro Manila Subway and North-South Commuter Railway.

Sionil José.
cinema: The Golden Ages of Philippine Cinema (Lino Brocka: "Manila in the Claws of Light", Ishmael Bernal: "Himala"); contemporary auteur Lav Diaz (Golden Lion winner at Venice for "The Woman Who Left"); internationally acclaimed director Brillante Mendoza (Cannes Best Director for "Kinatay").
sports: Basketball is an absolute national religion (PBA - Philippine Basketball Association is the oldest professional basketball league in Asia; basketball hoops found in every rural barangay); Boxing (Manny Pacquiao - historic eight-division world champion and global sporting legend); Weightlifting (Hidilyn Diaz made history by winning the Philippines' first-ever Olympic Gold medal at Tokyo 2020); Gymnastics (Carlos Yulo won historic double Olympic Gold medals in floor exercise and vault at Paris 2024); Pole Vault (EJ Obiena, world #2); Billiards (Efren "Bata" Reyes - greatest pool player of all time).
media: GMA Network, ABS-CBN (digital and broadcast content powerhouse), TV5, Philippine Daily Inquirer, The Philippine Star, and digital outlets Rappler and Inquirer.net.
clothing: Barong Tagalog (impeccably embroidered, lightweight formal sheer shirt made from Piña pineapple fiber or Jusi silk, worn untucked over an undershirt by men for formal occasions); Baro't Saya and Maria Clara dress with butterfly sleeves (Terno, popularized by national fashion) for women.
crafts: Piña cloth weaving (luxurious handwoven fabric from pineapple leaf fibers, UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage candidate), Inabel handwoven textiles of Ilocos, T'nalak abaca cloth woven by T'boli dream weavers, capiz shell lamps and windowpanes, and Paete woodcarving.

flagDescription: A horizontal bicolor of royal blue (top, symbolizing peace, truth, and justice) and crimson red (bottom, courage and patriotism), with a white equilateral triangle at the hoist (equality and fraternity) bearing a golden sun with eight rays (representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain) and three golden five-pointed stars in each corner of the triangle (representing the three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao); uniquely, during times of war, the flag is flown upside down with the red stripe on top.
coatOfArmsDescription: A shield featuring an eight-rayed golden sun and three five-pointed golden stars on a white chief, divided vertically into blue (bearing the American bald eagle) and red (bearing the lion rampant of Spain), with a scroll below inscribed "Republika ng Pilipinas".

travelNotes: Remarkably warm, friendly, and English-speaking population; visa-free entry for up to 30 days for citizens of over 150 countries; domestic air travel (via Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific) connects major island hubs seamlessly; island-hopping via outrigger Bangka boats is iconic; tropical sun and sea conditions are best between December and May.
shortSummary: The Philippines is an enchanting tropical archipelago of 7,641 islands in Southeast Asia, celebrated for its emerald rice terraces, powder-white sand beaches, world-renowned marine biodiversity, the warm resilient spirit of Bayanihan, and passionate musical and sporting excellence.
geography: Spanning 300,000 km² across Southeast Asia. Highest point: Mount Apo (2,954 m in Mindanao - sacred dormant stratovolcano); lowest point: Philippine Sea / South China Sea (0 m; Philippine Trench reaches -10,540 m at Galathea Depth). Longest river: Cagayan River (Rio Grande de Cagayan, 505 km in northern Luzon) / Rio Grande de Mindanao. Climate: Tropical maritime; hot and humid year-round; divided into the dry season / Tag-init (December to May) and wet monsoon season / Tag-ulan (June to November), with frequent Pacific typhoons.
economy: Economy with GDP nominal of $470 billion (approx. 2026) ($3,960 per capita). Leading sectors: Services 61% (Business Process Outsourcing / BPO, banking, retail, and tourism), Industry & Manufacturing 29%, Agriculture & Fisheries 10%. Main industries: Business Process Outsourcing (BPO / IT-BPM - global capital for voice customer service and healthcare analytics, employing >1.7 million professionals and generating >$38 billion annually), Electronics and semiconductor assembly (supplying automotive and computing components), Shipbuilding and drydocks (Subic Bay, Cebu - 4th largest shipbuilder worldwide), Food, beverage, and beer processing (San Miguel Corporation), Mining and nickel ore extraction (world's #2 producer of mined nickel for EV batteries), Remittance financial services and mobile fintech (GCash, Maya). Key exports: Semiconductor devices and electronic integrated circuits, Business process outsourcing and IT services (> $38 billion), Nickel ores and concentrates, Fresh and processed bananas and pineapples, Coconut oil and copra, Automotive ignition wiring sets, Machinery and optical equipment.
culture: Rich cultural traditions featuring cuisine (Celebrated for its unique balance of sweet, sour, and salty flavors: Chicken or Pork Adobo (national dish: meat braised in a marinade of cane vinegar, soy sauce, crushed garlic, black peppercorns, and bay leaves), Sinigang (comforting sour tamarind soup simmered with pork, shrimp, or fish, water spinach / Kangkong, radishes, and green long chilies, repeatedly voted world's best soup), Lechon (whole pig roasted over open charcoal with glass-crisp skin and succulent meat, praised by Anthony Bourdain as the "best pig ever"), Sisig (sizzling platter of minced pork jowl and ears seasoned with calamansi, onions, and chili peppers, topped with an egg), Kare-Kare (oxtail and tripe stew in rich peanut sauce served with fermented shrimp paste / Bagoong), Pancit Canton (stir-fried noodles with meat and vegetables), Lumpia (crispy spring rolls), and Halo-Halo (iconic shaved ice dessert layered with sweetened beans, coconut jelly, Ube purple yam halaya, leche flan, and evaporated milk).), traditional music and dance (Kundiman (traditional soulful lyric love songs expressing deep longing and patriotism); Kulintang (ancient bronze gong chime ensemble of Mindanao, UNESCO); OPM (Original Pilipino Music - vibrant acoustic ballads, pop, and rock: Eraserheads, Regine Velasquez, SB19 - global P-pop powerhouse); world-class choral traditions (Philippine Madrigal Singers).; Tinikling (national folk dance: dancers skip gracefully between two clapping bamboo poles imitating the movements of the Tikling bird); Singkil (regal Maranao royal dance over criss-crossing bamboo poles enacting the Darangen epic, UNESCO); Pandanggo sa Ilaw (balancing oil lamps on heads and hands).), literature (Dr. José Rizal's revolutionary masterworks written in Spanish: "Noli Me Tángere" (Touch Me Not) and "El Filibusterismo"; Francisco Balagtas's epic poem "Florante at Laura"; Nick Joaquin (National Artist for Literature: "The Woman Who Had Two Navels"); contemporary poetry and fiction by F. Sionil José.), and sports (Basketball is an absolute national religion (PBA - Philippine Basketball Association is the oldest professional basketball league in Asia; basketball hoops found in every rural barangay); Boxing (Manny Pacquiao - historic eight-division world champion and global sporting legend); Weightlifting (Hidilyn Diaz made history by winning the Philippines' first-ever Olympic Gold medal at Tokyo 2020); Gymnastics (Carlos Yulo won historic double Olympic Gold medals in floor exercise and vault at Paris 2024); Pole Vault (EJ Obiena, world #2); Billiards (Efren "Bata" Reyes - greatest pool player of all time).).

headOfState: Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani
legislature: Consultative Assembly (Shura Council / Majlis ash-Shura: 45 members, established by the 2004 constitution; in late 2024, constitutional amendments approved shifting to appointed council)
constitution: Approved by overwhelming national referendum in 2003, promulgated in 2004; updated by national referendum in October 2024 to strengthen national unity and constitutional governance
latestElections: First legislative elections for the Shura Council in October 2021; constitutional referendum in October 2024 approving revised governance frameworks
politicalSituation: Under Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar leverages its immense wealth and diplomatic prestige as an indispensable international mediator, notably brokering high-stakes negotiations between the United States, Israel, and Hamas, and facilitating humanitarian prisoner swaps worldwide. Domestically, Qatar is executing the $30+ billion North Field East and North Field South LNG expansion projects to increase national LNG output by 85% to 142 million tonnes annually by 2030, while building on the historic success of the FIFA World Cup 2022 to diversify into knowledge, AI, tourism, and global sports hosting.
foreignRelations: Major non-NATO ally of the United States (hosts the forward headquarters of US Central Command / CENTCOM and Al Udeid Air Base, the largest US air base in the Middle East); world-class mediator in global conflicts; member of the GCC, Arab League, and OPEC (withdrew to focus on natural gas); leading investor worldwide through the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA).
military: Qatar Armed Forces (Qatari Emiri Land Force, Qatari Emiri Air Force with Rafale, Eurofighter Typhoon, and F-15QA fighter jets, Qatari Emiri Navy; major modern joint defense coordination).
internationalOrgs: GECF (Gas Exporting Countries Forum - headquartered in Doha)
adminDivisions: 8 municipalities (baladiyat): Doha, Al Rayyan, Al Wakrah, Al Khor, Umm Salal, Al Daayen, Al Shamal, and Al Shahaniya
history: Settled since the Bronze Age (evidenced by the Kassite purple dye industry on Al Khor Island in the 2nd millennium BC), Qatar was famed in the ancient world for pearl diving, camel breeding, and boat building. Pliny the Elder referred to the inhabitants as "Catharrei". Qatar was influenced by the Dilmun civilization and embraced Islam in the 7th century under Caliph Abu Bakr. In the 18th century, families of the Bani Utbah settled at Zubarah, transforming it into a flourishing regional pearling and merchant port (Al Zubarah Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site). In the mid-19th century, Sheikh Mohammed bin Thani established the Al Thani Dynasty, signing a historic treaty with Britain in 1868 that recognized Qatar as a distinct political entity. His son, Sheikh Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani, defeated Ottoman forces at the Battle of Al Wajbah in 1893, unifying the tribes and earning the title "Founder of the State of Qatar". Following the collapse of the natural pearling industry in the 1930s due to Japanese cultured pearls, Qatar discovered commercial oil at Dukhan in 1939. In 1971, Qatar achieved full sovereign independence from Great Britain. In the late 20th century, Qatar discovered the colossal North Field (the largest non-associated natural gas field in the world). In 1995, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani (the "Father Emir") took power, launching monumental liquefied natural gas (LNG) export infrastructure with ExxonMobil, founding the global news network Al Jazeera in 1996, creating the Qatar Foundation and Education City, and winning the bid to host the FIFA World Cup 2022. Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani ascended the throne in 2013.
recentEvents2020_2026: Qatar hosted the historic FIFA World Cup 2022 in November–December 2022, universally acclaimed as one of the best-organized and most spectacular tournaments in history, played across eight architectural stadiums connected by the driverless Doha Metro. In January–February 2024, Qatar hosted and won the AFC Asian Cup 2023, retaining its continental championship. Between 2023 and 2026, Qatar played a pivotal global role mediating hostage releases and ceasefire diplomacy in the Israel-Hamas war, expanded the North Field gas mega-projects toward 142 million tonnes per annum, and passed constitutional amendments in October 2024 to reinforce state unity and efficiency.

etiquette: Warm greetings with handshakes and light nose-touches (Khabra) among close male friends; offering and accepting coffee and dates with the right hand; polite deferral to elders and hosts; conservative public dress code respecting Islamic values in shopping malls and public venues.
nationalIdentity: A blend of maritime pearling and Bedouin tribal chivalry, proud Islamic faith, world-leading energy sovereignty, philanthropic global generosity, sports diplomacy, and cutting-edge cultural and educational patronage.

art: Qatar Museums network (spearheaded by Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad Al Thani, making Qatar one of the world's premier art buyers and cultural destinations); Museum of Islamic Art (MIA); Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art; monumental public sculptures (Richard Serra's "East-West/West-East" in the Brouq desert, Urs Fischer's "Lamp Bear" in Hamad Airport).

Pei's geometric limestone fortress on the water), Qatar National Library (Rem Koolhaas), futuristic city of Lusail (Lusail Towers and Katara Towers resembling crossed scimitar swords), and Souq Waqif (meticulously restored mud-rendered traditional coral stone architecture).
literature: Historical maritime oral poetry (Nabati poetry celebrating desert life and falconry); modern literature by Abdulaziz Al-Mahmoud (historical novels: "The Corsair", "The Holy Sail"); contemporary Qatari poets and novelists.
cinema: Doha Film Institute (DFI - leading financier of world cinema and independent Arab directors, funding Oscar-nominated and Cannes-winning films worldwide); Ajyal Film Festival.

politicalSituation: Under King Salman and visionary Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), Saudi Arabia is undergoing a historic socioeconomic metamorphosis through "Vision 2030". The Kingdom has dismantled decades of social restrictions (permitting women to drive, re-opening cinemas, curating major arts and music festivals, and introducing modern tourism e-Visas), diversified state revenues, empowered the Public Investment Fund (PIF - sovereign wealth fund managing >$925 billion), launched transformative giga-projects (NEOM, Red Sea Project, Diriyah, Qiddiya), and won hosting rights for World Expo 2030 in Riyadh and the FIFA World Cup 2034.
foreignRelations: G20 member; leader of OPEC+ and founding member of the GCC and Arab League; Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques (spiritual heart of the Islamic world); brokered historic diplomatic normalization with Iran via Chinese mediation in 2023; strategic defense partnership with the United States; expanding trade ties with China, India, and the Global South.
military: Saudi Arabian Armed Forces (Royal Saudi Land Forces, Royal Saudi Air Force with F-15SA and Eurofighter Typhoon fleets, Royal Saudi Navy, Royal Saudi Air Defense with Patriot missile defense, and the elite Saudi Arabian National Guard).
adminDivisions: 13 administrative provinces (mintaqat): Riyadh, Makkah, Madinah, Eastern Province, Asir, Tabuk, Hail, Northern Borders, Jazan, Najran, Al Bahah, Al Jawf, and Qassim
history: The Arabian Peninsula has been inhabited since prehistoric times. It is the sacred birthplace of Islam: in 610 AD in Mecca, Prophet Muhammad received the divine revelations of the Holy Quran, later migrating (Hijra) in 622 AD to Medina to establish the first Islamic state, which expanded within decades to become a global civilization stretching from Spain to India. Mecca and Medina remain the two holiest cities in Islam. Modern Saudi history comprises three distinct states: the First Saudi State (Emirate of Diriyah, 1727–1818) founded through the alliance of Imam Muhammad bin Saud and religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab; the Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd, 1824–1891) based in Riyadh under Turki bin Abdullah; and the Third Saudi State founded by King Abdulaziz Al Saud (Ibn Saud). In 1902, young Abdulaziz captured the Masmak Fortress in Riyadh, systematically reunifying the tribes of Nejd, Al-Hasa, Asir, and the Hejaz, officially proclaiming the unified Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on September 23, 1932. In 1938, commercial petroleum was struck at Dammam No. 7 ("Prosperity Well") by the California Arabian Standard Oil Company (which became Saudi Aramco), transforming the desert kingdom into an energy superpower. King Faisal (1964–1975) modernized state education, media, and foreign policy, famously executing the 1973 oil embargo. Successive kings (Khalid, Fahd, Abdullah) expanded the Two Holy Mosques to accommodate millions of pilgrims. In 2015, King Salman ascended the throne, elevating Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in 2017 to spearhead Vision 2030.
recentEvents2020_2026: Between 2022 and 2026, Saudi Arabia achieved unprecedented global visibility: hosted historic Chinese and Arab summits in Riyadh, restored formal diplomatic ties with Iran in March 2023 under Chinese auspices, was selected to host World Expo 2030 in Riyadh, and secured uncontested hosting rights for the FIFA World Cup 2034. In the economic realm, Saudi Aramco achieved record annual profits, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) transformed global sports (investing heavily in the Saudi Pro League, LIV Golf, and ATP/WTA tennis), commercial tourism expanded at UNESCO AlUla, and construction accelerated across the giga-projects of NEOM (The Line, Oxagon, Trojena ski resort) and the Red Sea destination.

name: Singapore

Periodic transboundary agricultural smoke haze from regional peat fires
environmentalIssues: Scarcity of natural freshwater solved through the "Four National Taps" (local catchments, imported water from Johor, NEWater high-grade recycled water, and desalination)
Vulnerability to sea-level rise (countered by raising coastal reclamation minimums to 5 meters)
Urban heat island effect mitigated by "City in Nature" greening
